To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a neural strategy is more effective than a standard method in SH3 domain interaction specificity inference.
a neural network is more precise than a PSSM in detecting SH3 domain interactants and that the neural network performance depends on the number of true positives in a benchmark set.

1) a neural network is a suitable tool to predict SH3 domain specificity; 2) a neural network can identify general binders and domain specific interactors from a peptide population that is characterized by a sufficient number of true positives in its training sets; and 3) this capability can improve peptide selection for array experiments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an inference strategy for the detection of SH-3 domain specificity.
the design and the validation of a novel approach for SH3 domain-peptides interaction inference, which can be extended to the study of other PRM families and to other protein families.
the definition of a computational strategy for the identification of putative binding peptide sequences that can be used in experimental settings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a neural network model can be more effective in the detection of binding peptide sequences for SH3 domains.
a neural classifier, properly trained, can provide a more reliable inference strategy for SH3 domain-peptides interaction specificity.

a neural strategy is more suitable than PSSM for the inference of the SH3 domain-peptides interaction specificity, and that the use of neural networks is a promising approach for protein-protein interaction prediction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a neural strategy can provide a valuable support to experimental biologists in the search for SH3 ligands.
neural networks can provide a valuable support for experimental approaches in the study of protein-protein interactions.

a neural network is more suitable than PSSM for the prediction of the SH3 domain-peptidic interactors, and that the use of such a model can improve the efficiency of the SH3 binding peptide selection for high-throughput experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a neural strategy can be a valid and reliable approach to the inference of SH 3 domain-peptide interactions.
the neural network approach is an effective tool for SH3 domain-peptides interaction specificity inference.
neural networks are a valuable computational tool in the study of protein-protein interactions.
